notes: Phase 2 M1 source pack for Nigeria. Hardening I (NG-B1/B6/B7) preserved. Hardening II (2026-09-09) adds NG-B2/NG-B3 resident and non-resident FCY-account evidence. Primary account-law substrate: FEMMPA 1995 Part II; CBN CDD Regulations 2023 category eligibility; CBN 2025 NRNOA/NRNIA circular. CBN Foreign Exchange Manual Fourth Edition (announced on the CBN Reforms page as launched 2026-05-15) was not pinned as a downloadable CBN-hosted PDF in this review — detailed ordinary-vs-export domiciliary operational access rules from that Manual are missing-authority and are not adopted from press/law-firm summaries.

sources.notes: Operational current guidance and e-form. Uses '$10,000 or more' / 'equal to or greater than' wording. Hardening I-B preserves this as the operational operator (>=) alongside the statutory MLPPA operator (>); no reconciling primary instrument was pinned.

sources.label: CBN circular — Introduction of Non-Resident Nigerian Ordinary Account (NRNOA) and Non-Resident Nigerian Investment Account (NRNIA)
sources.notes: Hardening II: diaspora Non-Resident Nigerian account classes. Policy is without prejudice to Memorandum 17 of the CBN Foreign Exchange Manual (2018). Does not establish a comparative proposition that non-residents generally operate more freely than residents.

sources.label: CBN Reforms and Initiatives — official reforms chronology page
sources.notes: Hardening II temporal meta only: records 2025-01-10 NRNOA/NRNIA introduction and 2026-05-15 launch of Foreign Exchange Manual Fourth Edition. Does not itself contain memorandum-level domiciliary operating rules.

source_conflicts.detail: Money Laundering Act section 3(3) uses 'in excess of US$10,000' (operator >) while the current Nigeria Customs e-declaration form uses '$10,000 or more' / 'equal to or greater than $10,000' (operator >=). Hardening I-B bounded search found no later primary amending or interpretive instrument that formally reconciles the operators. Customs press language often restates 'exceeding', but the live e-form remains inclusive. Disposition: preserve dual operators; do not flatten > into >= or vice versa.
source_conflicts.wording_boundary: Statutory declaration trigger remains 'in excess of US$10,000'. Operational Customs e-form trigger remains 'US$10,000 or more'. Future wording must keep both roles distinct and must not invent a single reconciled operator.

missing_authorities.topic: current guideline exception under section 14 of the Foreign Exchange (Monitoring and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act for physical naira import/export
missing_authorities.reason: Hardening I-B bounded primary search (CBN-hosted FX Manual PDF; current Monetary/Credit/Foreign Trade guidelines PDF; CBN circulars expressly implementing FEMMPA s.14 traveller exceptions) did not pin a currently operative official instrument establishing a live numeric traveller exception threshold for physical naira notes. Historical CBN guideline language (for example older N10,000 declaration wording) and secondary press/law-firm summaries referring to N100,000 were treated as discovery aids only and were not adopted. Conclusion: numeric exception = not established.
missing_authorities.wording_boundary: Publish only the FEMMPA s.14 prohibition baseline plus the fact that any numeric traveller exception remains not established. Do not invent N10,000, N20,000, N100,000, or any other numeric NGN carriage/exception figure from secondary sources.

missing_authorities.topic: Foreign Exchange Manual Fourth Edition (2026) — ordinary vs export domiciliary operational access, Form A / remittance documentation, and cash-withdrawal rules for export-proceeds accounts
missing_authorities.reason: Hardening II bounded primary search located the CBN Reforms announcement of the Fourth Edition launch (2026-05-15) but did not pin a currently downloadable CBN-hosted PDF of the Manual text for memorandum-level ordinary-domiciliary, export-proceeds-domiciliary, or Form A rules. Press and law-firm summaries describing unfettered ordinary-domiciliary access, Form A removal, export-proceeds cash-withdrawal bans, and related operational detail were treated as discovery aids only and were not adopted. Conclusion: FX Manual 2026 operational domiciliary access rules = not established from pinned primary text in this review.
missing_authorities.wording_boundary: Do not adopt ordinary-vs-export domiciliary operational access, unrestricted-access, Form A, or export-proceeds cash-withdrawal propositions from secondary summaries. Prefer FEMMPA statutory opening rules, CDD category eligibility, and the pinned NRN circular until the Manual PDF is pinned.
